pay.conditions: Official page: all accepted stories are paid at competitive rates based on the amount and type of work. Rates, deadlines, scope and kill fees (if any) are discussed if they are interested. A pitch itself creates no right to payment.
pay.timing: Typically within 30 days via Shortlist, if assigned.

wordCount.display: Most stories 1,500–2,500 words

response.label: They cannot respond to every pitch

whatTheyWant: The world’s biggest, most neglected moral and technological problems.

Official core areas: global poverty and public health; catastrophic and existential threats; animal welfare and factory farming; progress studies; AI and biotechnology; philanthropy and altruism; moral philosophy.

A couple of paragraphs: unique angle, why now, why you, pre-reporting and source access, proposed headline and word count, a line about yourself, links to similar published work. All in the email body.
whatTheyDontWant: Attachments. AI-written pitches.
Q&As unless the subject is hard to get.
Traditional reviews. Shopping roundups. Manuscripts or academic papers.
Already-written pieces — they rarely accept them.
requirements: Pitch in the body, no attachment
opportunities.rights: Not fully stated on the pitch page. Assigned work goes through a Shortlist agreement.
howToSubmit: Read https://www.vox.com/how-to-pitch-vox-pitching-guidelines.
Email futureperfectfreelance@vox.com with the pitch in the body.

wordCount.display: Generally 2,500–5,000 words

response.label: They cannot respond to every enquiry

opportunities.title: True first-person stories and story-poems
opportunities.seoTitle: Chicken Soup for the Soul: $250 if published, AI banned
opportunities.excerpt: Chicken Soup for the Soul pays $250 plus 10 free copies if they publish your true first-person story in a book — not for submitting. Official: writers from anywhere, English. AI and AI-assisted work (including Grammarly) are banned. Current official book topics have deadlines in September–November 2026.

eligibility.summary: Official FAQ: they publish English-language stories from people around the world. You do not have to live in the United States.

pay.conditions: Official: they do not pay for submissions. If they publish the story in a book you are paid $250 one month after the book is published, plus ten free copies. You also get half-price cases of that book. A story is not paid unless it is selected and you sign their permission release.
pay.timing: One month after publication of the book.

wordCount.display: Recommended maximum 1,200 words; no official minimum. Longer pieces are rarely read.

response.label: No rejection letters. If you have not heard 60 days before the book’s on-sale date, they probably passed.

deadline.display: Current official topics (check the page — they change): Count your blessings 15 Sept 2026; Random acts of kindness 30 Sept 2026; Humorous stories 15 Oct 2026; Married/couples 30 Nov 2026

whatTheyWant: A true first-person story with a beginning, middle and end, starting in the action.
Heartwarming, funny or extraordinary ordinary-life moments. Not a sermon, essay, eulogy, term paper, politics piece, biography or newspaper-style article about a stranger.
Poems only if they tell a story.
Submit only to a listed official book topic.
whatTheyDontWant: AI-generated or AI-assisted work. Official page names Grammarly and says do not use AI at all.
Fiction. Previously published work except a small local publication or your own blog.
Book manuscripts from the public. Title ideas from the public.
Stories that do not match a listed book topic.
requirements: True story, first person, usually ≤1,200 words
Match a current official book topic
opportunities.rights: If selected you sign their standard permission release. Broader rights language is not copied here because the rest of that agreement is not fully quoted on the public guidelines page.
howToSubmit: Pick a topic on https://www.chickensoup.com/story-submissions/possible-book-topics — only use deadlines on that page.
Submit via the official form. Success screen is the only confirmation.
Simultaneous submissions are allowed if you say so in the comments or email webmaster@chickensoupforthesoul.com.
